newsitem.title: UK: Gold price to claw its way higher - Anglo official.
newsitem.headline: Gold price to claw its way higher - Anglo official.

text.p: A slide in gold prices to three-year lows has ended but the market would remain wary of central bank selling, a top offical of Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said on Tuesday.

Eventually, prices would rise as the market confronts fundamentals that show an increasing gap between supply and demand, chairman of corporate affairs Clem Sunter told Reuters on the sidelines of an investment conference in London.
"My view is that it has bottomed out," he said.

Perceived and actual liquidation of a portion of the 36,000 tonnes of gold held by central banks and other players was behind the recent slide in gold values, said Sunter, until earlier this year chairman of the gold and uranium division of Anglo, the world's biggest gold producer. "I don't think it's producer hedging that's holding the price down," Sunter said. "What has caused the continuing indifferent gold price is stock changes."
"That (36,000 tonnes) equals 18 years of supply. A small ripple in that can have a huge effect on the market," he said.
The market would remain jittery as the European Union moves towards strict economic criteria for a single currency, stoking fears that countries may offload gold to reduce budget deficits.
But fears of huge selling by central banks were overdone since they would not sell to the extent that it greatly ran down the value of their remaining holdings.
"There could be a short-term depressing effect of potential rationalisation (in Europe), but it doesn't eliminate the gap that is developing. At some stage that must surface," he said.
By the turn of the century, the gap between supply and demand is expected to have grown to 400 tonnes, Sunter said.
"Incremental supply in the 1990s is nowhere near that in the 1980s when a lot of huge open-pit mines were established in Australia and Canada," he said.
Current low prices will stimulate demand in China and the Far East, thereby lending support to the market, he added.
